[RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Not every essence can receive a word: essences are infinite, and what cannot be distinctly apprehended cannot be assigned a name.
[RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The more urgent a meaning is to express, the more fitting it is to coin a word for it; commands, prohibitions, generality, and particularity illustrate this need.
[RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | A common word cannot name a meaning hidden from most people: common الحركة denotes bodily movement, not the obscure cause proposed by some theologians.
[RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Accordingly, الحركة names the transition itself, while knowledge and power name being knowing and being capable, not hidden causes of those states.
[RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Meaning is the mental image intended by a speaker, not external things in themselves; external objects are meant only secondarily.
[RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The difference between plant sweetness and sugar-candy sweetness lacks a dedicated word, so it can be described only relationally; a coined term would make verbal definition possible.
[RAZI-FULL:v1p31/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | A person cannot name a private inner state for listeners who have never conceived it; if a group first conceived that state and coined a term, they could define it verbally.
[RAZI-FULL:v4p82#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · اليهود والنصارى | reports | Jews and Christians argue that abrogation entails either God's ignorance or His misleading people: an unqualified command lasts once, a temporary one is not abrogated, and revoking an explicitly permanent command implies either a change in knowledge or deception.
[RAZI-FULL:v4p82#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · اليهود والنصارى | reports | They further argue that qibla directions are equally God's creation, so changing between them lacks a change in benefit and is purposeless, which they say is inconsistent with divine wisdom.
[RAZI-FULL:v4p82#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Razi identifies the challenge to the qibla change as an argument by which these groups seek to discredit Islam, and turns to explaining the wording before answering it as the Quran does.
[RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · القفال | reports | Al-Qaffal says the future form can describe a past utterance when it is repeated; reports say the criticism had already been voiced when the verse came down.
[RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Alternatively, the verse predicts the criticism before it occurs, demonstrating knowledge of the unseen, easing its hurt, and placing the answer ready for the Prophet.
[RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | A fool cannot distinguish benefit from harm and abandons sound judgment; error in religion is more harmful than worldly error, so every unbeliever is foolish.
[RAZI-FULL:v4p83/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · ابن عباس، مجاهد | reports | They identify the critics as Jews, who expected the Prophet's agreement on the qibla to lead to full agreement; after the change they said he had returned to his forefathers' way.
